item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 031717
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sat Oct 3 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Nolo, located several hundred miles west-northwest of the main
Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Rachel, located a few hundred
miles south-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form late this weekend or
early next week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression is likely to form during the middle to
latter portion of next week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward to northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Public Advisory Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Sat Oct 03 2026 
610 
WTPZ33 KNHC 032053
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM MST Sat Oct 03 2026
 
...RACHEL CONTINUES MOVING SLOWLY WEST-NORTHWEST...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.8N 112.5W
ABOUT 270 MI...435 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...80 MPH...130 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...977 MB...28.85 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 19.8 North, longitude 112.5 West. Rachel is moving
toward the west-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this slow motion
is expected to continue through tonight. A west to west-northwest
motion is then expected Sunday through the middle of next week,
with a gradual increase in forward speed.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 80 mph (130 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Some weakening is forecast during the next day or so, with 
some slight restrengthening possible on Monday. 
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 977 mb (28.85 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will continue to affect the coast
of west-central Mexico through the weekend and the Baja California
Peninsula through Monday. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Blake

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Sat Oct 03 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 032054
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM MST Sat Oct 03 2026

Satellite imagery suggests that Rachel has formed a larger eye this 
afternoon, with the inner eyewall fading away on the latest 
infrared data.  Intensity estimates have dropped slightly, and
latest subjective Dvorak CI number from TAFB was 
4.5/77 kt, but the Final T-number was 4.0/65 kt. This aligns well 
with most UW-CIMSS objective satellite intensity estimates, which 
range from 63 to 77 kt. Based on a compromise of these data, the 
initial intensity is lowered to 70 kt.

The initial motion continues west-northwestward, or 300/4 kt. 
Rachel's slow motion over the next two days will be governed by a 
ridge extending southwestward from a mid- to upper-level high over 
the western United States. Rachel is forecast to accelerate 
slightly after 60 h, continuing on a west to west-northwestward 
trajectory through the remainder of the forecast period. The 
updated NHC track forecast is largely unchanged from the previous 
advisory and roughly follows the corrected-consensus (HCCA) aid 
through 120 h. 

Rachel is anticipated to gradual weaken through the next 24 h due 
to an unfavorable environment of moderate northeasterly vertical 
wind shear, dry mid-level air, and cooler sea surface temperatures 
(SSTs) associated with Hurricane Polo's cold wake. As Rachel 
moves west of the wake, environmental conditions should allow 
for some re-intensification after the weekend through 72 h. 
However, beyond 72 h, Rachel will encounter an even drier air mass, 
with mid-level relative humidity values dipping below 40 percent. 
At the same time, SSTs will drop below 26 C, likely expediting the 
weakening trend through the remainder of the forecast period. The 
new forecast is very similar to the previous one.
